target.role: fresh whole-journey belonging and placement discovery for STRANGE GAIT
target.position: Whole journey: before the opener, between every non-protected pair, or after the tail. Preserve only Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer; Truth in Noise → Transparency remains available.
target.purpose: Test one current collaborative mutation, one emerging broken-rhythm release and three overlooked structural catalogue cuts. Character changes are allowed; admission still requires purposeful transition, local-run and long-form effect.

sourceWindows: CURRENT 2026 / WISDOM TEETH: https://wisdomteethuk.bandcamp.com/album/bborn-again — all five tracks were screened. PPP — Pez was retained from the official exact-track description of glitched Perlon reconstruction and Piezo sound-design disruption inside a collaborative record that moves in disparate but connected directions.

EMERGING / DISCOS EXTENDES: https://discosextendes.bandcamp.com/album/medusas — all four tracks were screened. BLEID — Kerosene was retained from the official exact-track description of a rising-tempo roller driven largely by percussion, inside an EP explicitly moving from steady 4/4 toward broken rhythms.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / RHYTHM SECTION INTERNATIONAL: https://ra.co/reviews/21200 — all five tracks on Mallard's Verte were screened. Mallard — Surface was retained from the exact review documenting a pivot between 3/4 at 90 BPM and 4/4 triplet time in the 120s.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / MONNOM BLACK: https://ra.co/reviews/34879 — all three tracks were screened. Vanquished — M. Bison was retained from the exact review documenting broken techno with dual acid leads, a piano-vamp breakdown and a reassembled return.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / MAMA TOLD YA: https://ra.co/reviews/35791 — all twenty compilation tracks were screened through Resident Advisor's review. Cerrot — The light was retained from the exact-track description of an off-kilter, lumbering polyrhythm.

ADDITIONAL WINDOWS: current Ilian Tape releases, Wisdom Teeth's Nagoya compilation, PHTM VA 4, Livity Sound and Timedance-adjacent catalogues, BLEID's label catalogue, Second Storey, Seph, Breaka, Deadbeat, Yard and Peverelist/Kowton catalogue reviews were screened. Previous Run 53–72 candidates, release-level-only claims and weaker repetitions were excluded.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 45 named tracks and releases across current releases, adjacent/emerging artists and labels, and overlooked catalogue windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–72 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.
No lead was promoted for recency, reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. Album-level claims were not converted into exact-track behaviour.

Energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, phrase structure, harmonic relation, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown. Source-reported meter and BPM relationships are evidence, not flow verdicts.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Mallard — Surface: strongest exact metric case, documented as pivoting between 3/4 at 90 BPM and 4/4 triplet time in the 120s.
2. Vanquished — M. Bison: strongest exact internal-transformation case, moving from broken techno into piano-vamp breakdown and back into a reassembled whole.
3. PPP — Pez: strongest current collaborative mutation, officially framed as a glitched Perlon reconstruction with sound-design disruption.
4. BLEID — Kerosene: emerging broken-rhythm cut officially described as a rising-tempo, percussion-driven roller.
5. Cerrot — The light: overlooked compilation cut with an exact review documenting an off-kilter, lumbering polyrhythm.
